requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: A persistent sysctl policy sets accept_redirects to 0 for all, default, and per-interface scopes. Runtime values were zero immediately after application and remained zero for all observed interfaces after a verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets accept_source_route to 0 for all, default, and per-interface scopes. Runtime values were zero immediately after application and for every observed interface following the reboot.

overall_summary: Both required IPv4 hardening controls are satisfied. Direct observations show the settings applied across all current interfaces and persisted through a confirmed node restart with healthy network recovery. The mandatory restart evidence is complete and consistent with the lifecycle snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and applying the sysctl policy was required for the task, and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. All other commands were read-only checks or bounded recovery observations. Afterward, package health remained intact, no services were failed, and no suspicious exposure or abandoned temporary residue appeared. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered networking and policy state; lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate it.
